name: United Arab Republic
alt: Egypt as the United Arab Republic (1961-1971)

predecessors.name: Republic of Egypt
predecessors.text: Egypt, the Egyptian region of the union

predecessors.name: Second Syrian Republic
predecessors.text: Syria, the Northern region of the union

successors.name: Arab Republic of Egypt
successors.text: Egypt less the Israeli-occupied Sinai; the name 'Arab Republic of Egypt' was adopted in September 1971

successors.name: Republic of Syria
successors.text: Syria, seceded on 28 September 1961 after a coup

ledger.x: 1958: Egypt and Syria unite as the United Arab Republic under Nasser.
1958: Syria joins the union as its Northern region.
February 1958: Egypt sends troops into the Halaib Triangle.
February 1958: Egypt withdraws its troops from the Halaib Triangle 'the same month'.
1959: Egyptian administration of the Gaza Strip.
28 September 1961: a coup in Damascus ends the union.
6 June 1967: Egyptian administration of Gaza ends.
June 1967: Israel occupies the Sinai Peninsula.
September 1971: Egypt becomes the Arab Republic of Egypt.

wars.name: Six-Day War
wars.outcome: Israeli victory, 5-10 June 1967: Israel occupied the Sinai and the Gaza Strip (from Egypt), the West Bank (from Jordan) and the Golan Heights (from Syria), 'a total of 70,000 km2'; Egypt and Jordan accepted a cease-fire on 8 June, Syria on 9 June, signed with…

wars.name: Halaib crisis of 1958
wars.outcome: Egyptian troops entered the triangle in February 1958 and withdrew the same month; the sovereignty dispute continued, with Sudan holding or sharing the area until Egypt moved in during 1994-1995.

wars.name: 1961 Syrian coup d'état and secession
wars.outcome: Syria left the union on 28 September 1961; Nasser called off a landing at Latakia and recognised the secession on 5 October.

certainty.note: Egyptian and Syrian frontiers follow treaty and armistice lines; the exceptions are the Halaib Triangle (disputed with Sudan) and the Gaza Strip (administered under the 1949 armistice, not annexed).

The Sinai front is a cease-fire line along the Suez Canal after June 1967 (the page says Israeli forces reached 'various points along the length of the Suez Canal'), so that edge is only as sharp as the line held; the Halaib Triangle stays…
